results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 72 aligned outline summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p76, including p58 in Channels and p37-p38 in Retention after Attribution); the five callouts are unaligned framing.

Only Trade-offs ¶1 (p64) was marked two_ideas (table framing / masking). Its first sentence is the explanation of the trade-offs table that precedes it, and the spec's controlling idea for p64 is exactly 'decisions have limits, masking needs the most care'; the paragraph develops that one idea, so it is not a second controlling idea.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and concepts to S1/S4, channels to S2, architecture and safety to S1/S3, leads and routing to S4, attribution to S5 (p53 lead-count monitoring to S6's 'measure the path'), retention to S1, worked example and CA view to S3/S4/S6.

Each table and figure is introduced or followed by a sentence saying what it shows (conversation-vs-lead table, channel table with four observations, component table, gate-checks table, delivery-channel table followed by the pull/push paragraph, retention table followed by 'The last row is the reason...', baseline, trade-offs and verticals tables; Figures 1-6 have explanatory captions). Quotations (OLX, Discord, Rightmove, Autotrader, Kleinanzeigen, CoStar, Zillow, Adevinta, EECC) each carry a sentence of interpretation.

results.quote: The table shows how channels, recipients, fraud, qualification, routing and outcome data change by vertical
results.finding: The declared transition into Vertical Differences is elaboration carrying over 'general trade-offs'. The section opens straight on its table and then 'The table shows how...change by vertical', with no reference to the trade-offs just discussed, so the boundary does not express the elaboration; both flow readers could not say why this section follows Trade-offs.

All other section and paragraph boundaries express their declared relationship and pick up the declared known information (e.g. 'Ingrid's second question...' into Concepts, 'Whatever the channel' into Architecture, 'The step between stored and shown' into Safety, 'With the conversation and its gate in place' into Leads, 'Both objects leave data behind' into Retention, 'The second case was a counting problem, not a safety problem', 'The last row is the reason', 'The eight failure modes above point to decisions').

results.quote: Ingrid's second question, what a lead is, needs definitions first.
results.finding: Both readers stopped here: naming the second question first made them expect the chapter to answer it first, while it answers safety (the first question) next. The definitions serve both questions; the sentence should say so.

results.quote: Even "immutable" messages carry metadata that changes, and that shapes the store.
results.finding: The opening repeats the previous paragraph's 'messages are immutable in content but their metadata changes', and the OLX evidence states it a third time; readers re-read looking for a new point.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-B item 1 (same sentence, read as a restatement)

results.quote: The portal controls the states up to Delivered; everything after Acknowledged depends on data from the professional's systems.
results.finding: The lead states are never listed in the prose; the caption leaves Acknowledged unassigned and the Concepts table's 'qualified' state conflicts with qualification at the moment of contact, so readers went back to the Concepts table to follow 'Two things in Figure 4 are easy to miss'.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-B item 3 (same passage: the text never lists the lead states)

results.quote: Lead counts are also an operational signal
results.finding: The Adevinta Artemis monitoring paragraph sits between attribution and disintermediation and is about monitoring, not attribution; both readers said it interrupts the line from attribution to disintermediation and would sit better under 'Measure the path' or Failure Modes. The prose expresses the declared additional_support, so the difficulty is the paragraph's position in the spec.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-B item 4 (same paragraph, same 'out of place' point)

results.quote: with Keybridge as the fourth, receiving leads from many portals
results.finding: Both readers re-read this sentence: Keybridge's role as a receiving software vendor, not a brand with a contact system, is packed into a subordinate clause and appears here for the first time, although the scene already said Veldmark 'ran four contact systems'. Introducing Keybridge's role where the four systems are first mentioned, or in its own sentence here, would fix it.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-B item 6 (same sentence, Keybridge's role packed into a clause)

results.quote: That gives 13 + 1 + 5 = **19 leads** from the 23 contacts that Motorvane's 2027 reporting counted as leads
results.finding: Both readers re-read the Golf replay arithmetic: the merged booking is described twice (inside the e-mail sentence and again under bookings), and 'the 23 contacts that Motorvane's 2027 reporting counted as leads' can be read as describing the 19.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-A item 9 and reader-flow-B item 8 (same passage, the Golf replay arithmetic)

results.quote: The table shows how channels, recipients, fraud, qualification, routing and outcome data change by vertical
results.finding: Neither reader could say why Vertical Differences follows Trade-offs ('not obvious' for A; 'only partly clear' for B). The section has no opening sentence connecting it to the trade-offs, so its position is unexplained in the prose.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-B section 2, Vertical Differences (same section, position only partly clear)

results.quote: messages inside the chat can be written by the chat partner
results.finding: Reader A had to re-read to see that the quoted "Kleinanzeigen" refers to messages claiming to come from the platform.

results.quote: Veldmark set a budget of **150 ms at p99**
results.finding: Reader B could not tell whether these Veldmark parameters (150 ms, 24-hour fail-closed rule, 14 million messages a day) were already in place or are what the forum adopted in May 2027, since the worked example later presents them as decisions.

results.quote: is the other side of attribution.
results.finding: Reader B did not see why disintermediation is 'the other side of attribution'; the link is asserted, not shown (e.g. outcomes the portal cannot see). Reader A found the placement 'clear enough, though looser', so this is not corroborated.

results.quote: The same rule withholds the account
results.finding: Reader B stopped to reconcile the nine other sellers reached before the report with the 37 messages withheld afterwards; the replay does not say how the two sets relate.

results.quote: (the Golf's removal arrived 26 hours after the sale)
results.finding: Reader B met a new fact about the Golf case that appears in neither the scene nor the replay and checked whether it had been missed.

results.quote: they generalize the four Veldmark's forum recorded.
results.finding: Reader B slowed to parse the elliptical 'the four Veldmark's forum recorded' as 'the four decisions Veldmark's forum recorded'.
Reader A found no clear antecedent for 'points the same way'; the direction (share the platform early) is only in the bold lead-in.

results.quote: a little above search's peak-to-average ratio of about 3.4
results.finding: Reader A had to compute 600/160 to see what 'a little above' meant, relying on a ratio from another chapter; a minor stop.

The chapter's owned and does_not_know terms are explained at or before first body use: conversation, lead, lead routing and connection in Concepts; DMS on first use; ADF XML in the delivery table; Rightmove's RTDF ('the API through which UK agency software exchanges data'); pull vs push and exactly-once on the lead ID in the pull/push paragraph; hot partitions, per-participant inbox index and idempotency keys in the storage paragraphs; GDPR legitimate interest and the EECC 'interpersonal communications service' in the privacy paragraph. Terms the flow readers stopped on (Common Ground, the neutrality decision) are in already_knows or glossed in place.

The introduction opens with a direct claim about the contact as the marketplace's unit of output and moves to the two-object split, the chapter's place in Part VI and a roadmap; it is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary opening, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion answers Ingrid's two questions with one design principle and hands off to payments; it does not open with 'in conclusion', add new evidence or subtopics, or end on a bare restated thesis.

p75 joins the two halves no single section joins ('keep the conversation and the lead apart, and give each its own control') and says why it matters: 'A platform that merges the two objects can neither stop a phishing link in time nor defend an invoice'.

The conclusion returns to the opening claim ('The conversation is where the platform still sees both parties') and to both scene cases (the check that protects Femke; the Golf's 23 contacts becoming 19 leads), as callback.to requires.

The cold reader of the introduction reproduced the section order from the roadmap (cases, definitions, channels, path and gate, lead life to attribution, retention, replay, trade-offs/verticals/failure modes/CA view/questions), the evidence (dated OLX, Discord, Rightmove, Autotrader, CarGurus, Zillow, CoStar, Adevinta sources, EU law, fictional Veldmark) and the declarative handbook tone. Its open questions are about details the body supplies.

The reader placed a synchronous gate between stored and shown with a 150 ms p99 budget, four verdicts, fail-closed for links/payment details from new accounts and a domain-age rule that withholds the link, with asynchronous scoring withdrawing messages and warning recipients; and a versioned lead rule with one deduplication rule across channels, stable lead IDs and acknowledged push delivery, turning 23 contacts into the same 19 leads with calls and bookings counted. Matches expected.

The reader of the opening alone listed the moment of contact split into conversation and lead, why the chapter opens Part VI, and the sections in the expected order, with the expected evidence (OLX, Discord, Rightmove, Autotrader, CarGurus, Zillow, CoStar, Adevinta, EU law, fictional Veldmark).
The reverse outline, written without the spec, lists the spec's controlling ideas in the spec's order for all 72 aligned units.

The reader said conversation and lead are different objects with different owners and retention, that counting the chat store makes chat changes alter billing retroactively and misses calls/bookings, and proposed a lead service with a versioned rule, its own store and stable lead IDs; and that only the conversation service stores content, with the data platform receiving message events with identifiers and timings, because every copy must be found, secured and deleted. Matches expected.

The reader assigned the vendor a pull contract that delivers at least once and often twice by design (Rightmove's 15/20-minute windows) with deduplication on the stable lead ID by the vendor, and the dealer group push delivery with retries until acknowledged and the same lead ID each time so the portal owns exactly-once, both on the same lead contract. Matches expected.
